newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK SAYS READY TO START REPO AUCTIONS.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK SAYS READY TO START REPO AUCTIONS.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Monday that it was ready to launch repo auctions as soon as the liquidity situation in the country's banks called for them.
"We can do repo auctions at any time now...the central bank and the banks are ready for them," Arvydas Kregzde, the director of the Bank of Lithuania's market operations department, told Reuters.

"We have signed agreements with seven banks and an agreement with an eighth bank is almost ready...almost all of the banks in the country have expressed an interest in participating in the auctions," he said.
"We will hold the first one when it is warrented by the liquidity situation in the banks...it won't happen this week but will certainly happen next month," he added.
The central bank says that the repo auctions are needed to soak up excess liquidity in the country's banking sector.
The auctions are the first step in the bank's two to three-year plan to regain the monetary policy instruments it lost when Lithuania adopted a currency board arrangement in the spring of 1994.
Under the system, the central bank guarantees that it will keep one dollar in reserve for every four litas in circulation, freezing the exchange rate at that level.
